data.one_liner: Static metaprogramming tool to define and execute custom code-generating annotations in-project.
data.what_it_does: Allows developers to create custom code generators by subclassing annotation classes like ClassAnnotation directly within their project. It leverages code_builder to generate code outputs dynamically via build_runner without authoring separate standalone generator packages. Generated outputs are emitted to .g.dart or customizable target files using an isolated execution runner.
use_when: You want custom code generation rules (such as custom data classes or serialization) tailored specifically to your project.
You want to avoid the boilerplate and overhead of creating a separate generator package with custom Builders.
You need in-project annotations that can read declaration metadata and parameters directly to build output ASTs.
avoid_when: Standard existing code generators like freezed or json_serializable already meet all your project needs.
You want completely pure build phases without spawning dynamic isolate runners during compilation.
strengths: Enables defining annotations and their code generation logic side-by-side in the same project.
Simplifies generator authoring by passing code_builder types and target metadata directly to an apply method.
Supports multiple custom generation targets and lifecycle hooks (runBefore/runAfter).
weaknesses: Code defining annotations must be syntactically valid and compilable before build_runner can execute, sometimes requiring file separation from target models.
Debugging code generator logic requires setting up custom IDE run configurations for build_runner's entrypoint script.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding build_runner as a dev dependency, configuring @CodeGen() at the library level, and running `dart run build_runner build`.

alternatives.name: source_gen
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick source_gen when writing reusable, industry-standard Generator and Builder packages intended for pub.dev distribution.
